extraction_text: King Drupada (木柱王) harbors intense anger and seeks a Brahmin to help him have a son who can kill Drona.

attributes.relationships: Drupada seeks revenge against Drona, considering his existing sons inadequate for this purpose.

extraction_text: Drupada travels along the Ganges River and reaches a sacred Brahmin settlement.

attributes.location: Sacred Brahmin settlement near Ganges and Yamuna rivers

extraction_text: Drupada encounters two ascetic Brahmins, Yaja and Upayaja, who are studying the Vedas.

attributes.relationships: Yaja and Upayaja are brothers from the Kashyapa lineage, both are learned Brahmins.

extraction_text: Drupada approaches the younger brother Upayaja, serves him diligently, and flatters him to gain his favor.

attributes.action: Drupada follows Upayaja, speaks pleasing words, and fulfills his desires to gain his help.

extraction_text: Drupada asks Upayaja what sacrifice he should perform to have a son who can kill Drona, offering ten million cows and other desired items as reward.

attributes.offer: Ten million cows and any other desired items in exchange for performing the sacrifice.

extraction_text: Upayaja initially refuses Drupada's request, but Drupada continues to serve him for a year.

attributes.duration: One year of continued service by Drupada

extraction_text: After a year, Upayaja explains to Drupada why he refused, citing his brother Yaja's impurity from picking up fallen fruit without checking cleanliness and eating leftover food without discrimination.

attributes.reason: Upayaja considers Yaja impure due to his actions, implying this affects their suitability for the sacrifice.

extraction_text: King Drupada (referred to as '国王' or '木柱王') approached Yaja (耶阇) for help after being defeated by Drona (德罗纳).

attributes.reason: Defeat by Drona, desire for revenge

extraction_text: King Drupada explained his defeat by Drona, describing Drona's unmatched skills and power.

attributes.details: Drona is the chief teacher of the Kuru clan, possesses Brahmin power, and uses powerful weapons

extraction_text: King Drupada requested Yaja to perform a sacrifice to grant him a son who could kill Drona.

attributes.offer: Eight thousand cows initially, then ten million cows
attributes.purpose: To obtain a son capable of killing Drona

extraction_text: Yaja agreed to perform the sacrifice and forced his younger brother Upayaja (小耶阇) to assist, despite Upayaja's reluctance.

attributes.action: Yaja compelled Upayaja to help with the sacrifice

extraction_text: Upayaja informed King Drupada that the sacrifice would grant him a son with extraordinary qualities.

attributes.promise: The son would be heroic, radiant, and powerful, shaped as the king desired

extraction_text: King Drupada specified his desire for a son who could kill Drona and provided all necessary items for the sacrifice.
During the sacrifice, Yaja called for the queen (王后), wife of King Drupada, to come forward.

attributes.summons: Yaja summoned the queen to receive the fruit of the sacrifice

extraction_text: The queen hesitated, citing she was still adorned and needed time, but Yaja insisted the sacrifice was ready.

attributes.interaction: The queen delayed, Yaja urged her to come immediately

extraction_text: Yaja performed a sacrifice by offering cooked oblations into the sacrificial fire.
A divine-looking boy emerged from the sacrificial fire, with fiery complexion, fierce appearance, wearing celestial crown and armor, carrying weapons, and riding a chariot.
An invisible great spirit in the sky proclaimed that this prince would dispel fear, win glory for the Panchalas, remove the king's sorrow, and was born to kill Drona.
A princess of Panchala emerged from the center of the altar, with dark complexion, lotus-like eyes, beautiful form, and divine fragrance.
An invisible voice proclaimed that this dark beauty would cause the destruction of Kshatriyas and fulfill the gods' mission, bringing great terror upon Kshatriyas.

relationships: Draupadi destined to cause Kshatriya destruction

extraction_text: The daughter-in-law of King Drupada saw the children and asked Yaja to let them know she was their only mother.
Yaja agreed to please the king, and learned Brahmins gave names to the children: the boy was named Dhrishtadyumna and the girl was named Draupadi.
Drona, son of Bharadvaja, took Dhrishtadyumna to his palace to teach him martial arts, considering fate unavoidable and to preserve his own reputation.

relationships: Despite prophecy of Dhrishtadyumna killing Drona
